html:
Theodora was a Byzantine empress who, as regent for her young son, ended iconoclasm for good in 843. Born around 815 in Paphlagonia to a family of Armenian origin, she married Emperor Theophilos in 830. He was the last emperor to oppose icons, though she honoured them in private.

When Theophilos died in 842 she became regent for Michael III, then two years old. With the help of officials and the new patriarch Methodios, she called a synod in Constantinople in March 843 that restored icons and condemned their enemies, while sparing her husband's memory. The first Sunday of Lent, when the change was celebrated, is still kept as the Feast of the Triumph of Orthodoxy.

Her regency also persecuted the Paulicians, a dualist sect in the east, and many were killed. In 856 Michael and her brother Bardas pushed her from power, and she ended her life in a convent. The Orthodox church honours her as a saint.
